title: Working with Strings 🔗
description: Slice, dice, and combine strings – learn indexing, slicing, and more.

slides.title: String Concatenation & Repetition ➕✖️
slides.content:
# Combining Strings

You can join strings with the `+` operator (concatenation) and repeat them with `*`:

```python
first = "Hello"
second = "World"
greeting = first + ", " + second + "!"   # "Hello, World!"
laugh = "ha" * 3                        # "hahaha"
```

But careful: you can only concatenate strings with strings, not with numbers directly.

quizData.question: What is the result of `"Py" + "thon"`?
quizData.explanation: Strings are merged without any extra spaces unless you add them.

slides.title: String Indexing 🔢
slides.content:
## Accessing Individual Characters

Each character in a string has a **position**, starting at 0. Use square brackets to retrieve it:

```python
word = "Python"
print(word[0])   # P
print(word[1])   # y
print(word[-1])  # n (last character, negative index)
print(word[-2])  # o
```

Indices go from 0 to `len(s)-1`. Negative indices count from the end.

slides.title: Indexing Demo
slides.codeSnippet:
fruit = "strawberry"
print('First char:', fruit[0])
print('Last char:', fruit[-1])
print('Third char:', fruit[2])

quizData.question: If `s = "Data"`, what is `s[3]`?
quizData.explanation: Indices: D=0, a=1, t=2, a=3. So s[3] is 'a'.

slides.title: Slicing Strings ✂️
slides.content:
## Extracting Substrings

Slicing uses `[start:stop:step]`. It returns a portion of the string:

```python
s = "Hello, World!"
print(s[0:5])    # Hello (start at 0, stop before 5)
print(s[7:])     # World! (from index 7 to end)
print(s[:5])     # Hello (from start to 5)
print(s[::2])    # Hlo ol! (every second char)
print(s[::-1])   # !dlroW ,olleH (reverse)
```

Remember: start is inclusive, stop is exclusive.

slides.title: Slicing in Action
slides.content: Try different slices on the word "Progly":
slides.codeSnippet:
app = "Progly"
print(app[0:3])   # Pro
print(app[3:])    # gly
print(app[::-1])  # ylgorP

slides.title: String Length & Membership 📏
slides.content:
## `len()` and `in`

Get the length of a string with `len()`:
```python
print(len("Hello"))   # 5
```
Check if a substring exists with `in`:
```python
print("ol" in "Hello")   # True
print("xyz" in "Hello")  # False
```

slides.title: Strings Are Immutable ⚠️
slides.content:
## Cannot Change in Place

Strings cannot be modified after creation. Trying to do `s[0] = 'X'` raises an error. Instead, you create a new string:

```python
s = "Hello"
# s[0] = 'J'   # ERROR!
s = 'J' + s[1:]   # 'Jello'
```
This immutability ensures data safety.
